summary: The Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Modernization Act of 2026 reauthorizes and updates housing assistance laws for Native Americans, Alaska Natives, and Native Hawaiians. The bill provides funding authorizations, increases operational flexibilities for tribes and housing entities, streamlines environmental reviews, establishes new homeless assistance programs and pilot initiatives, and updates loan guarantee programs.

affected_groups.effect: Gain increased flexibility over technical assistance funding, procurement policies, rent rules, and environmental reviews, alongside new grant opportunities and extended lease terms.
affected_groups.group: Indian tribes and tribally designated housing entities

affected_groups.effect: Benefit from reauthorized housing assistance, expanded homeownership and loan guarantee provisions, and targeted homeless assistance programs.
affected_groups.group: Native Hawaiian families and the Department of Hawaiian Home Lands

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for specialized rental assistance and supported housing under the Tribal HUD-VASH program.
Stand to benefit from dedicated pilot programs and continuum of care builds providing housing and supportive services.
affected_groups.group: Homeless Native Americans, Alaska Natives, and Native Hawaiians

key_provisions: Reauthorizes appropriations for programs under the Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Act of 1996 for fiscal years 2027 through 2033.
Streamlines and consolidates environmental review requirements, exempting certain activities and lowering regulatory burdens for housing projects.
Expands homeownership assistance eligibility by allowing recipients to serve families with incomes up to 120 percent of the area median income under specific conditions.
Extends the maximum leasehold interest on trust or restricted lands for housing purposes from 50 years to 99 years.

Establishes new programs and pilot initiatives, including the Tribal HUD-VASH rental assistance program for homeless or at-risk Indian veterans, the Tribal Homeless Assistance program, and the Tribal and Rural Continuum of Care Builds Program.

Exempts programs and projects assisted by the Secretary for Indian tribes, tribally designated housing entities, tribal organizations, and the Department of Hawaiian Home Lands from Build America, Buy America requirements.
Maintains the HUD Tribal Intergovernmental Advisory Committee as a formal government-to-government advisory body.

The bill provides funding authorizations, increases operational flexibilities for tribes and housing entities, streamlines environmental reviews, establishes new homeless assistance programs and pilot initiatives, and updates loan guarantee programs.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation has a substantial impact on federal housing policy for indigenous communities by updating long-standing block grant and loan guarantee structures, reducing administrative and environmental review hurdles, and creating dedicated channels to address homelessness and veteran housing needs in Indian country and Hawaii.
